newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end lower, Malaysian OTCs tumble.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end lower, Malaysian OTCs tumble.

text.p: The Singapore stock market ended lower on Thursday, weighed down by U.S. rate hike concerns and a poor corporate earnings outlook, dealers said.

"The market is unconvinced that a U.S. rate hike would not be translated to one here. If that happens, buying stocks could be less attractive and borrowing costs increase," said a dealer with a local house.

The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index ended 11.73 points down at 2,078.08 while the DBS 50 index fell 9.79 points to 521.74. Turnover was over 147 million shares, with 307 losers against 66 gainers.

Malaysian shares traded over the counter (OTC), like Rashid Hussain, Genting Bhd and Sime Darby, were among top losers after Kuala Lumpur exchange plunged 2.42 percent to 1,152.51 on weak technicals. The UOB OTC index lost 2.12 percent, or 26.66 points, to end at 1,230.37.
Foreign tranches of the Big Four banks -- UOB, OCBC, DBS and OUB -- were among the gainers on brighter 1997 earnings outlooks despite Singapore's economic slowdown.
SingTel fell to an 18 month low of S$2.76 before ending at S$2.81 after the company lost its monopoly on cellular phone and paging services.
